newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains forced down by strong sterling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains forced down by strong sterling.

text.p: LIFFE wheat was forced down to contract lows on Wednesday as sterling again forged higher against the mark.

One trader reckoned sterling's rise could have justified a bigger fall. "The market was quite resilient to hold up," he said. "It shows there are a lot of profit takers," he said, noting also shipper buying late in the day.

Active November wheat last traded 0.60 stg lower at 81.75 stg, having seen a new contract low of 81.40 stg. Its previous low was 81.50 stg seen on July 14. November volume was 135 of a total 355 lots.
Barley also fell in active trade. Active November last traded 0.75 stg lower at 77.50 stg. November volume was 169 of a total 203 lots.

As the first stages of the barley harvest proceed, harvest pressure, in the form of country sellers, helped it down, traders said. But it was well supported, particularly by players looking to buy barley and sell wheat, one trader said.
Physical market traders also noted that more harvest barley was starting to appear.
By late Wednesday, sterling/mark was steady a pfennig below peak of 3.0878, its strongest level since September 1989.
